name: Exploits
summary: Adversaries may buy, steal, or download exploits that can be used during targeting. An exploit takes advantage of a bug or vulnerability in order to cause unintended or unanticipated behavior to occur on computer hardware or software. Rather than developing their own exploits, an adversary may find/modify exploits from online or purchase them from exploit vendors. analytics.name: Analytic 1959
analytics.guidance: Much of this activity will take place outside the visibility of the target organization, making detection of this behavior difficult. Detection efforts may be focused on behaviors relating to the use of exploits (i.e. Exploit Public-Facing Application, Exploitation for Client Execution, Exploitation for Privilege Escalation, Exploitation for Stealth, Exploitation for Credential Access, Exploitation of Remote Services, and Application or System Exploitation).

telemetry.basis: ATT&CK detects relationship → detection strategy → analytic → log-source component reference
telemetry.planning_note: The upstream guidance describes limited target visibility. These are conditional investigation inputs, not direct victim-side detection of preparation. Simulator-side logs do not prove defender visibility.
